source_refs.note: Exercise 12.2, Question 4: find c so that the limit at x = -1 exists (book p.234). Answer key PDF 310: c = -1.

blocks.prompt: 4 If \[f(x) = \begin{cases} x + 2, & x \le -1 \\ c + 2, & x > -1 \end{cases}\]find \(c\) so that \(\lim_{x \to -1} f(x)\) exists.
blocks.explanation:
Yeh "constant find karo" wala sawal hai. Shart yeh di gayi hai ke \(x = -1\) par limit exist kare.
Limit tab hi exist karti hai jab LHL aur RHL barabar hon. Is shart se \(c\) ki ek equation ban jayegi.
Plan: dono taraf ki limits \(c\) ke saath nikalein, barabar rakhein, aur \(c\) solve karein.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(x \le -1\) ke liye \(f(x) = x + 2\), aur \(x > -1\) ke liye \(f(x) = c + 2\).
Humein find karna hai: \(c\) ki woh value jis se \(\lim_{x \to -1} f(x)\) exist kare.
Tareeqa: Limit exist karne ki shart: \(\lim_{x \to -1^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to -1^+} f(x)\). Yani dono taraf se function ek hi number ki taraf jaye.

Left hand limit nikalein
\[\lim_{x \to -1^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to -1^-} (x + 2)\]
\[= -1 + 2 = 1\]
Kyun: \(-1\) se left (\(-1.01\), \(-1.001\)) \(x \le -1\) wala pehla tukra lagta hai.

Right hand limit nikalein
\[\lim_{x \to -1^+} f(x) = \lim_{x \to -1^+} (c + 2)\]
\[= c + 2\]
Kyun: \(-1\) ke right function \(c + 2\) hai, jis mein \(x\) hai hi nahi; yeh ek constant hai. Constant ki limit wahi constant hoti hai.
Dhyan dein: Yahan \(c\) koi variable nahi jo badle; yeh ek fixed number hai jo humein dhoondna hai.

Dono ko barabar rakh kar solve karein
\[c + 2 = 1\]
\[c = 1 - 2 = -1\]
Kyun: Sirf isi value par dono taraf ki limits barabar hongi. Koi aur value lein, maslan \(c = 0\), to RHL 2 hoga aur LHL 1, limit exist nahi karegi.

Tasdeeq
\[c = -1:\ c + 2 = 1\]
\[\text{LHL} = \text{RHL} = 1\]
Kyun: \(c = -1\) rakhne se dono taraf 1 aata hai, is liye limit exist karti hai aur 1 hai. Saath hi \(f(-1) = 1\) bhi hai, to function yahan continuous bhi ban jata hai.
